notes.text: The handwritten sheet has the heading “Décompositions n-aires d’un espace topologique”, the oblique underlined marginal label “Version II”, and opening numbering “1.1.”. A pale pencil 31 at the bottom left is retained as archive numbering. No separate author page number or date is visible. There are eight displayed formula groups and no drawing or arrow diagram.

The page introduces a “décomposition binaire” through a pair of closed distinct parts. The first family symbol retains pi/Pi uncertainty, with pi first from its lower cap and curved right foot. Omega’s parenthesis uses ens, followed by two vertically paired marks retained as colon|à and then deux éléments. The cancelled ensembles is represented before parties; the elevated mark in dé/de/d’e remains unresolved. The complete word indiciellement is resolved.

The manuscript labels the union expression (1), the nonempty-member expression (2), and the pair exclusion (2′). The following prose reads “et implique que X...” and “et même card X ≥ 2, puisque l’on a supposé”. The next live display records distinct Sigma members and its written si clause. These statements were read for local symbol consistency; no proof of them was performed.

The word distinctes and the later distinctness display helped locate the live inequality. The crop retains uncertainty about the older marks under the first Sigma and comparison. The final epsilon-prime is resolved from the matching upper return and downward lower bend in the preceding primed epsilon, with the prime independently visible. R3’s r-prime alternative is recorded in the apparatus. The compact display label remains 3|s|wedge; sequence alone does not decide it.

The author writes “On n’exclut pas le cas où on aurait une inclusion”, followed by Sigma with prime-index epsilon contained in Sigma with epsilon. The next line reads “ce qui équivaut, par (1), à la relation”, followed by Sigma^epsilon=X. The open-right subset shape, both superscripts, the reference (1), and the equality were read in half b; no mathematical equivalence was checked in this run.

The word hémisphéres/hémisphères and équateur are underlined. The tiny second accent favours acute by its slight rightward rise, while grave remains possible. The cancelled article is resolved as la. In (4), a low omega is overwritten by a taller epsilon in the lower index, and the Sigma superscript is visibly omega. H’s note reports this omega, although its displayed formula uses epsilon. S row SA01-K81-04 proposes epsilon from the definitions. This run confirms the written omega and does not insert that proposed correction. The mismatch between the family’s epsilon indices and the omega exponent prompted crop inspection; no mathematical proof was performed.

The final prose reads “où on aurait E=...” and “ce qui indique”. The d ascender and following i dot settle indique. Two interlinear additions are present: (epsilon in omega), attached beside the final Sigma, and “complémentaires l’un de l’autre, donc”, whose brace point attaches after sont and before à la fois. H identifies both additions in its note; its running text places the second group before sont. The final donc in the addition remains uncertain because its last strokes are compressed. The last main-line clause reads “donc que X est disconnexe.”

No explicit author question, dated check or separate verification note was reported in the three readings. The page has been read independently three times, all complete returns compared, and every reader/witness disagreement adjudicated from local crops. C’s twelve doubts are covered: four resolved and eight retained. The family-case and ens punctuation loci add two uncertainties. No OCR, external research, compilation or proof check was performed.
